def-cm-oscillator-model-and-phase-system:
## Definition

Let $m>0$, $c\ge0$ and $k\in\mathbb R$ be given real numbers, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $f:I\to\mathbb R$ be continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]). The **damped driven oscillator model** with data $(m,c,k,f)$ is the second-order equation

$$m\,x''(t)+c\,x'(t)+k\,x(t)=f(t),\qquad t\in I .$$

A **solution** of the model on an interval $J\subseteq I$ with nonempty interior is a twice differentiable $x:J\to\mathbb R$ such that the identity holds for every $t\in J$, derivatives being ordinary real derivatives ([[def-derivative]], [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]). The model is called **homogeneous** when $f\equiv 0$, **undamped** when $c=0$, and **strictly damped** when $c>0$.

The **phase-plane system** of the model is the first-order system on the open set $I\times\mathbb R^2$ ([[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]) with right-hand side

$$G_f:I\times\mathbb R^2\longrightarrow\mathbb R^2,\qquad G_f(t,x,v):=\Bigl(v,\ \frac{f(t)-c\,v-k\,x}{m}\Bigr).$$

Here $\mathbb R^2$ is the **phase plane**, with coordinates $(x,v)$, where $x$ is the **displacement** and $v$ the **velocity**. If $x$ is a solution of the model on $J$, then $t\mapsto(x(t),x'(t))$ solves $z'=G_f(t,z)$ on $J$; conversely, if $t\mapsto(x(t),v(t))$ solves $z'=G_f(t,z)$ on $J$, then $v=x'$ and $x$ is a solution of the model on $J$. For the homogeneous model the right-hand side is written $G_0(x,v)=(v,-(cv+kx)/m)$.

The **characteristic polynomial** of the model is

$$p(\lambda):=m\lambda^2+c\lambda+k,$$

with **discriminant** $\Delta:=c^2-4mk$. When $k>0$ define the **undamped frequency** $\omega_0:=\sqrt{k/m}$, the **damping rate** $\gamma:=c/(2m)$ and, when $4mk>c^2$, the **damped frequency** $\omega:=\sqrt{k/m-\gamma^2}=\sqrt{4mk-c^2}/(2m)$; the corresponding square roots are the nonnegative real ones.
def-cm-averaging-data-and-averaged-field:
## Definition

Let $n\ge1$, let $P>0$, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, and let $f:\mathbb R\times O\to\mathbb R^n$ be continuous ([[def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity]]) and continuously partially differentiable in its second variable ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]), and suppose $f$ is **$P$-periodic in time**, that is

$$f(t+P,x)=f(t,x)\qquad\text{for all }(t,x)\in\mathbb R\times O .$$

The **average** of such an $f$ is the map

$$\bar f:O\longrightarrow\mathbb R^n,\qquad \bar f(x):=\frac1P\int_0^Pf(s,x)\,ds,$$

where the integral is the componentwise Riemann integral of the continuous curve $s\mapsto f(s,x)$ over the compact interval $[0,P]$ ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]], [[def-interval]]); it is well defined and finite for every $x\in O$ because that curve is continuous. The **oscillatory part** of $f$ is $f-\bar f$, and the **deviation** of $f$ is

$$g:[0,P]\times O\longrightarrow\mathbb R^n,\qquad g(t,x):=\int_0^t\bigl(f(s,x)-\bar f(x)\bigr)\,ds .$$

Because $\int_0^Pf(s,x)-\bar f(x)\,ds=P\bar f(x)-P\bar f(x)=0$ by linearity and additivity of the integral ([[thm-additivity-over-subintervals]]), the formula $g(t+kP,x):=g(t,x)$ for $k\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\in[0,P)$ defines a unique extension, again written $g$, to all of $\mathbb R\times O$; it satisfies $g(t+P,x)=g(t,x)$ and $g(0,x)=0$ for all $(t,x)$, and on $[0,P]$ it is the integral displayed above.

The **averaged (or reduced) system** of $f$ for a parameter $\varepsilon>0$ is the autonomous first-order system on $O$

$$y'(t)=\varepsilon\,\bar f(y(t)).$$
def-cm-parameter-dependent-action-angle-:
## Definition

Let $\varepsilon>0$, let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ and $S\subseteq\mathbb R$ be intervals with nonempty interiors ([[def-interval]]), and let $h:J\times S\to\mathbb R$ and $k:J\times\mathbb R\times S\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^2$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), with $k$ $2\pi$-periodic in its second variable:

$$k(I,\theta+2\pi,s)=k(I,\theta,s)\qquad\text{for all }(I,\theta,s)\in J\times\mathbb R\times S .$$

The **transformed Hamiltonian** of the datum is

$$K(I,\theta,s):=h(I,s)+\varepsilon\,k(I,\theta,s),$$

its **frequency function** is

$$\omega(I,s):=\partial_Ih(I,s),$$

its **angle average** is $\langle k\rangle(I,s):=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}k(I,\theta,s)\,d\theta$, and, on the set where $\omega\ne0$, its **drift generator** is

$$g(I,\theta,s):=\frac{k(I,\theta,s)-\langle k\rangle(I,s)}{\omega(I,s)} .$$

The **branch vector field** of the datum is the map $\Phi:J\times\mathbb R\times S\to\mathbb R^3$,

$$\Phi(I,\theta,s):=\Bigl(-\varepsilon\,\partial_\theta k(I,\theta,s),\ \ \partial_Ih(I,\theta,s)+\varepsilon\,\partial_Ik(I,\theta,s),\ \ \varepsilon\Bigr),$$

and a **branch solution** on an interval $T\subseteq\mathbb R$ with nonempty interior is a differentiable $(I,\theta,s):T\to J\times\mathbb R\times S$ solving the first-order system $(I,\theta,s)'=\Phi(I,\theta,s)$ on $T$ in the sense of [[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]] ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). Partial derivatives are those of the ambient Euclidean coordinates.
lem-cm-convolution-differentiation:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]), let $t_0\in I$, let $g:I\to M_n(\mathbb R)$ be of class $C^1$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) and let $f:I\to\mathbb R^n$ be continuous ([[def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity]]). Define

$$F:I\longrightarrow\mathbb R^n,\qquad F(t):=\int_{t_0}^t g(t-s)f(s)\,ds,$$

with the oriented integral of [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]] and the matrix-vector product $g(u)f(s)$; the integrand is continuous in $s$, hence integrable on every compact subinterval. Then:

1. $F$ is differentiable at every interior point $t$ of $I$ ([[def-derivative]]) and

$$F'(t)=g(0)f(t)+\int_{t_0}^t g'(t-s)f(s)\,ds .$$

2. If moreover $g$ is of class $C^1$ and $g'$ is bounded on compact subintervals of $I$ (which holds automatically when $g$ is $C^2$), then $F$ is of class $C^1$ on the interior of $I$.
thm-cm-homogeneous-oscillator-solution-c:
## Statement

Let $m>0$, $c\ge0$ and $k>0$, and consider the homogeneous damped oscillator model $m\,x''+c\,x'+k\,x=0$ ([[def-cm-oscillator-model-and-phase-system]]), with characteristic polynomial $p(\lambda)=m\lambda^2+c\lambda+k$, discriminant $\Delta=c^2-4mk$, damping rate $\gamma:=c/(2m)$, and, when applicable, roots
$$\lambda_\pm:=\frac{-c\pm\sqrt\Delta}{2m}\ (\Delta\ge0),\qquad \lambda:=-\frac{c}{2m},\qquad \omega:=\frac{\sqrt{4mk-c^2}}{2m}\ (\Delta<0).$$

1. **Distinct real roots.** If $\Delta>0$, then $\lambda_+>\lambda_-$ are exactly the real roots of $p$, and a function $x:J\to\mathbb R$ on an interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ with nonempty interior is a solution of the model if and only if
$$x(t)=Ae^{\lambda_+t}+Be^{\lambda_-t}\quad(t\in J)$$
for some $A,B\in\mathbb R$.

2. **Double real root.** If $\Delta=0$, then $\lambda=-c/(2m)$ is the only root of $p$, and $x:J\to\mathbb R$ is a solution if and only if
$$x(t)=(A+Bt)e^{\lambda t}\quad(t\in J)$$
for some $A,B\in\mathbb R$.

3. **Complex conjugate roots.** If $\Delta<0$, then $\omega>0$, the roots of $p$ are $-\gamma\pm i\omega$, and $x:J\to\mathbb R$ is a solution if and only if
$$x(t)=e^{-\gamma t}\bigl(A\cos(\omega t)+B\sin(\omega t)\bigr)\quad(t\in J)$$
for some $A,B\in\mathbb R$.

4. **Initial data.** In each of the three cases and for every $(x_0,v_0)\in\mathbb R^2$ there is exactly one solution $x:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ with $x(0)=x_0$ and $x'(0)=v_0$. Its coefficients are
$$A=\frac{v_0-\lambda_-x_0}{\lambda_+-\lambda_-},\quad B=\frac{\lambda_+x_0-v_0}{\lambda_+-\lambda_-}\quad(\Delta>0),\qquad A=x_0,\ B=v_0-\lambda x_0\quad(\Delta=0),$$
$$A=x_0,\quad B=\frac{v_0+\gamma x_0}{\omega}\quad(\Delta<0).$$
prop-cm-oscillator-degenerate-and-repuls:
## Statement

Let $m>0$, $c\ge0$, let $k\le0$, and consider the model $m\,x''+c\,x'+k\,x=0$ ([[def-cm-oscillator-model-and-phase-system]]). In the three cases below, $x:J\to\mathbb R$ runs over solutions on intervals $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ with nonempty interior.

1. **Double zero root ($k=0$, $c=0$).** Then $x$ solves the model if and only if $x(t)=A+Bt$ for some $A,B\in\mathbb R$, and the unique solution with $x(0)=x_0$, $x'(0)=v_0$ is $x(t)=x_0+v_0t$.
2. **Simple zero root ($k=0$, $c>0$).** Then $x$ solves the model if and only if
$$x(t)=A+Be^{-ct/m}$$
for some $A,B\in\mathbb R$; the solution with $x(0)=x_0$, $x'(0)=v_0$ has $A=x_0+\frac{m v_0}{c}$ and $B=-\frac{m v_0}{c}$; every solution has the finite limit $A$ as $t\to+\infty$.
3. **One positive and one negative root ($k<0$).** Put $$\lambda_\pm:=\frac{-c\pm\sqrt{c^2-4mk}}{2m}.$$ Then $\lambda_-<0<\lambda_+$, both are real roots of the characteristic polynomial, and $x$ solves the model if and only if
$$x(t)=Ae^{\lambda_+t}+Be^{\lambda_-t}$$
for some $A,B\in\mathbb R$. In particular $t\mapsto e^{\lambda_+t}$ is the solution with data $x(0)=1$, $x'(0)=\lambda_+$, and it satisfies $e^{\lambda_+t}\to+\infty$ as $t\to+\infty$: the model has an unbounded solution growing exponentially on $[0,\infty)$.
cor-cm-variation-of-constants-for-linear:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$, let $A\in M_n(\mathbb R)$, let $t_0\in\mathbb R$ and $z_0\in\mathbb R^n$, and let $b:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^n$ be continuous ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]). Define the **matrix exponential**

$$E:\mathbb R\longrightarrow M_n(\mathbb R),\qquad E(t):=\sum_{k=0}^\infty\frac{t^k}{k!}A^k .$$

Then:

1. $E$ is well defined and of class $C^1$, with $E(0)=I_n$, $E(u+v)=E(u)E(v)$, $\frac{d}{du}E(u)=AE(u)=E(u)A$ for all $u,v\in\mathbb R$, and $\|E(u)\|\le e^{\|A\||u|}$ for the operator norm ([[def-operator-norm]]) subordinate to the Euclidean norm.
2. The map
$$z:\mathbb R\longrightarrow\mathbb R^n,\qquad z(t):=E(t-t_0)z_0+\int_{t_0}^tE(t-s)b(s)\,ds,$$
satisfies $z(t_0)=z_0$ and $z'(t)=A\,z(t)+b(t)$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$.
3. Uniqueness: if $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ is an interval with nonempty interior containing $t_0$ ([[def-interval]]) and $w:J\to\mathbb R^n$ is differentiable with $w'=Aw+b$ on $J$ and $w(t_0)=z_0$, then $w=z|_J$.
thm-cm-forced-oscillator-variation-of-co:
## Statement

Let $m>0$, $c\ge0$, $k\ge0$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $f:I\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. Fix $t_0\in I$ and data $(x_0,v_0)\in\mathbb R^2$. Let $g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be the (unique) solution of the homogeneous model with $g(0)=0$ and $g'(0)=1/m$.

Then:

1. There is exactly one solution $x:I\to\mathbb R$ of the forced model $m\,x''+c\,x'+k\,x=f$ with $x(t_0)=x_0$ and $x'(t_0)=v_0$, and it is of class $C^2$ on $I$.
2. If $x_h:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is any homogeneous solution with $x_h(t_0)=x_0$ and $x_h'(t_0)=v_0$ (it exists and is unique by [[thm-cm-homogeneous-oscillator-solution-classification]] and [[prop-cm-oscillator-degenerate-and-repulsive-cases]]), then
$$x(t)=x_h(t)+\int_{t_0}^tg(t-s)f(s)\,ds\qquad(t\in I).$$
cor-cm-forced-modal-oscillator-response:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$, let $M\in M_n(\mathbb R)$ be symmetric positive definite, let $K\in M_n(\mathbb R)$ be symmetric and non-negative, let $S:=M^{-1/2}KM^{-1/2}=O\Lambda O^{\mathsf T}$ with $O$ orthogonal and $\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$, $\lambda_i\ge0$ ([[thm-cm-quadratic-mode-decomposition]]), let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]), let $\varphi:I\to\mathbb R^n$ be continuous and let $t_0\in I$. Put

$$\psi(t):=O^{\mathsf T}M^{-1/2}\varphi(t),\qquad \omega_i:=\sqrt{\lambda_i}\ (\lambda_i>0),$$

and for a $C^2$ curve $q:I\to\mathbb R^n$ put $z:=O^{\mathsf T}M^{1/2}q$. Then:

1. $q$ solves the forced quadratic system $Mq''+Kq=\varphi$ on $I$ if and only if $z$ solves the decoupled forced system
$$z_i''+\lambda_iz_i=\psi_i\qquad(1\le i\le n)$$
on $I$.
2. For each $i$, the unique solution $z_i:I\to\mathbb R$ of the scalar equation in clause 1 with data $z_i(t_0)=\xi_i$, $z_i'(t_0)=\eta_i$ is
$$z_i(t)=\xi_i\cos\bigl(\omega_i(t-t_0)\bigr)+\frac{\eta_i}{\omega_i}\sin\bigl(\omega_i(t-t_0)\bigr)+\frac1{\omega_i}\int_{t_0}^t\sin\bigl(\omega_i(t-s)\bigr)\psi_i(s)\,ds\quad(\lambda_i>0),$$
$$z_i(t)=\xi_i+\eta_i(t-t_0)+\int_{t_0}^t(t-s)\psi_i(s)\,ds\quad(\lambda_i=0).$$
3. Consequently, for every initial datum $(q(t_0),q'(t_0))\in\mathbb R^{2n}$ there is exactly one solution $q:I\to\mathbb R^n$ of $Mq''+Kq=\varphi$ with that datum, and it is $q=M^{-1/2}Oz$ for the $z$ of clause 2.
thm-cm-forced-oscillator-sinusoidal-resp:
## Statement

Let $m>0$, $k>0$, $c\ge0$, let $f_0\in\mathbb R$ and $\Omega\ge0$, and consider the forced model $m\,x''+c\,x'+k\,x=f$ with $f(t)=f_0\cos(\Omega t)$ ([[def-cm-oscillator-model-and-phase-system]]). Put

$$D:=k-m\Omega^2+i\,c\,\Omega\in\mathbb C,\qquad \omega_0:=\sqrt{k/m}.$$

1. **Non-resonant response.** If $D\ne0$, then the function
$$x_p(t):=\operatorname{Re}\!\left(\frac{f_0e^{i\Omega t}}{D}\right)=f_0\,\frac{(k-m\Omega^2)\cos(\Omega t)+c\,\Omega\sin(\Omega t)}{(k-m\Omega^2)^2+c^2\Omega^2}$$
is a solution of the forced model on all of $\mathbb R$. Its amplitude about zero is $|f_0|/\sqrt{(k-m\Omega^2)^2+c^2\Omega^2}$.

2. **Resonance.** If $c=0$ and $\Omega=\omega_0$, then $D=0$ and
$$x_p(t):=\frac{f_0\,t\sin(\omega_0t)}{2m\omega_0}$$
is a solution of the forced model on all of $\mathbb R$; if $f_0\ne0$ then $x_p$ is unbounded on $[0,\infty)$.

3. **Transient decay.** If $c>0$, then $D\ne0$ for every $\Omega\ge0$, and every solution $x:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ of the forced model satisfies
$$x(t)=x_p(t)+x_h(t)$$
where $x_h$ is a homogeneous solution; consequently $x(t)-x_p(t)\to0$ as $t\to+\infty$ ([[def-limits-at-infinity]]) and $x$ is bounded on $[0,\infty)$.
prop-cm-oscillator-amplitude-maximum:
## Statement

Let $m>0$, $k>0$, $c>0$ and $f_0\ne0$. For $\Omega\ge0$ let

$$A(\Omega):=\frac{|f_0|}{\sqrt{(k-m\Omega^2)^2+c^2\Omega^2}}$$

be the amplitude about zero of the steady response of [[thm-cm-forced-oscillator-sinusoidal-response]] clause 1, and put

$$u_*:=\frac{k}{m}-\frac{c^2}{2m^2},\qquad \Omega_*:=\sqrt{u_*}\ \ \text{when }u_*>0 .$$

Then:

1. If $u_*>0$ (equivalently $c^2<2mk$), $A$ is strictly increasing on $[0,\Omega_*]$, strictly decreasing on $[\Omega_*,\infty)$, and its maximum on $[0,\infty)$ is attained at $\Omega_*$ and at no other point, with
$$A(\Omega_*)=\frac{2m|f_0|}{c\sqrt{4mk-c^2}} .$$
2. If $u_*\le0$ then $A$ is strictly decreasing on $[0,\infty)$ and its maximum on $[0,\infty)$ is attained at $\Omega=0$ and at no other point.
lem-cm-averaging-data-basic-bounds:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$, $P>0$, $O\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ open, and let $f:\mathbb R\times O\to\mathbb R^n$ be continuous, continuously partially differentiable in the second variable and $P$-periodic in time, with average $\bar f$, oscillatory part $f-\bar f$ and periodic deviation $g$ as in [[def-cm-averaging-data-and-averaged-field]] ([[def-interval]]). Let $x_0\in O$, $R>0$ with $\overline B(x_0,R)\subseteq O$ ([[def-metric-ball]]) and let $M,L\ge0$ satisfy

$$\|f(t,x)\|_2\le M,\qquad \|f(t,x)-f(t,y)\|_2\le L\|x-y\|_2\qquad(t\in\mathbb R,\ x,y\in\overline B(x_0,R)).$$

Then:

1. $\|\bar f(x)\|_2\le M$ and $\|\bar f(x)-\bar f(y)\|_2\le L\|x-y\|_2$ for all $x,y\in\overline B(x_0,R)$.
2. $g$ is $P$-periodic with $\|g(t,x)\|_2\le2MP$ for all $(t,x)$, and $\|g(t,x)-g(t,y)\|_2\le2LP\|x-y\|_2$ for all $t\in\mathbb R$ and $x,y\in\overline B(x_0,R)$.
3. $\partial_tg(t,x)=f(t,x)-\bar f(x)$ for every $(t,x)$; consequently $\|\partial_tg(t,x)\|_2\le2M$ and $\|\partial_tg(t,x)-\partial_tg(t,y)\|_2\le2L\|x-y\|_2$ on the stated sets.
4. $g$ has continuous first partial derivatives on $\mathbb R\times O$; its partial derivative in the second variable is $D_xg(t,x)=\int_0^t\bigl(D_xf(s,x)-D_x\bar f(x)\bigr)ds$, and $\|D_xg(t,x)\|\le2LP$ for $t\in\mathbb R$, $x\in\overline B(x_0,R)$, with $\|\cdot\|$ the operator norm on $M_n(\mathbb R)$ ([[def-operator-norm]]). In particular $g$ is totally differentiable at every point of $\mathbb R\times O$ ([[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]]).
thm-cm-finite-time-linearization-error-b:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with $0\in U$, let $F:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be continuous and locally Lipschitz in the state variable, and let $r>0$, $C\ge0$, $L\ge0$ and $A\in M_n(\mathbb R)$ satisfy $\overline B(0,r)\subseteq U$ ([[def-metric-ball]]) and

$$\|F(z)-Az\|_2\le C\|z\|_2^2,\qquad \|F(z)\|_2\le L\|z\|_2\qquad(\|z\|_2\le r).$$

Let $z_0\in\mathbb R^n$ with $\delta:=\|z_0\|_2>0$, let $T>0$ with $\delta e^{LT}<r$, and let $y:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^n$ be the solution of the linear system $y'=Ay$, $y(0)=z_0$ ([[cor-cm-variation-of-constants-for-linear-systems]]). Then:

1. The maximal solution $z$ of $z'=F(z)$, $z(0)=z_0$ is defined on $[0,T]$ and satisfies $\|z(t)\|_2\le\delta e^{Lt}$ for $t\in[0,T]$ ([[def-maximal-ode-solution]]).
2. For every $t\in[0,T]$,
$$\|z(t)-y(t)\|_2\le C\delta^2\int_0^te^{\|A\|(t-s)}e^{2Ls}\,ds\le C\delta^2\,t\,e^{(\|A\|+2L)t},$$
where $\|A\|$ is the operator norm of $A$ for the Euclidean norm ([[def-operator-norm]]).
thm-cm-averaging-for-fast-periodic-oscil:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$, $P>0$, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, and let $f:\mathbb R\times O\to\mathbb R^n$ be continuous, continuously partially differentiable in the second variable and $P$-periodic in time, with average $\bar f$ and deviation $g$ as in [[def-cm-averaging-data-and-averaged-field]]. Let $x_0\in O$, let $0<\rho<R$ with $\overline B(x_0,R)\subseteq O$ ([[def-metric-ball]]), and let $M,L\ge0$ satisfy

$$\|f(t,x)\|_2\le M,\qquad \|D_xf(t,x)\|\le L\qquad\bigl(t\in\mathbb R,\ x\in\overline B(x_0,R)\bigr),$$

$\|\cdot\|$ being the operator norm ([[def-operator-norm]]). Put

$$B:=2MP,\qquad B_1:=2LP,\qquad K:=e^{LA}\bigl[B+(LB+B_1M)A\bigr],$$

where $\varepsilon>0$ and $A>0$ are parameters. Suppose $y:[0,A/\varepsilon]\to\overline B(x_0,R-\rho)$ is a solution of the averaged system

$$y'(t)=\varepsilon\bar f(y(t)),\qquad y(0)=x_0 .$$

If $\varepsilon K<\rho$, then the solution $x$ of $x'(t)=\varepsilon f(t,x(t))$, $x(0)=x_0$ exists on all of $[0,A/\varepsilon]$ and satisfies, for every $t\in[0,A/\varepsilon]$,

$$\|x(t)-y(t)\|_2\le\varepsilon K=\varepsilon\,e^{LA}\bigl[B+(LB+B_1M)A\bigr].$$
thm-cm-adiabatic-invariant-drift-bound:
## Statement

Let $\varepsilon>0$, $A>0$, $\omega_0>0$, let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ and $S\subseteq\mathbb R$ be intervals with nonempty interiors, and let $h:J\times S\to\mathbb R$ and $k:J\times\mathbb R\times S\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^2$ with $k$ $2\pi$-periodic in its second variable ([[def-cm-parameter-dependent-action-angle-branch]], [[def-interval]]). Let $K\subseteq J$ and $S_0\subseteq S$ be compact intervals, let $s_0\in S_0$, and suppose

$$|\partial_Ih(I,s)|\ge\omega_0\qquad\bigl((I,s)\in K\times S_0\bigr).$$

Let $(I,\theta,s):[0,A/\varepsilon]\to J\times\mathbb R\times S$ be a branch solution of the branch vector field of the datum ([[def-cm-parameter-dependent-action-angle-branch]]) with $s(0)=s_0$, and suppose that for every $t\in[0,A/\varepsilon]$ one has $I(t)\in K$ and $s(t)\in S_0$. Then for every $t\in[0,A/\varepsilon]$,

$$|I(t)-I(0)|\le\varepsilon\Bigl[2\sup_{K\times[0,2\pi]\times S_0}|g|+A\sup_{K\times[0,2\pi]\times S_0}\bigl|\partial_Ig\,\partial_\theta k-\partial_\theta g\,\partial_Ik-\partial_sg\bigr|\Bigr],$$

where $g=(k-\langle k\rangle)/\partial_Ih$ is the drift generator of the datum.
